sourceInspection: Direct visual inspection of all 20 original Problems PNGs extracted by the existing safe ZIP reader. PNG hashes were verified against source-manifest.json. No Solutions entries opened.
evaluationType: same-assistant developmental coverage audit; author judgments, not independent grading or a solved-question rate
caseSourceBinding: Each case ID is bound to the exact path and PNG SHA-256 in the immutable frozen policy and CI source-manifest; do not replace a source or infer lengths from image scale.

sourceFacts: Incident unit direction is (i + sqrt(3) j)/2; reflected direction is (i - sqrt(3) j)/2.
One plane mirror; requested incidence angle.
sourceUnknowns: Mirror position and finite extent, source position and brightness are not given; they are unnecessary for the stated angular question.
cases.supportedSubset: Native plane reflection exists, but the audited standalone mirror-angle contract starts at two mirrors and is not a direction-pair inverse.
physicalInputsMissing: Native source/mirror placement and finite extent; no numeric apparatus is inferred.
cases.educationalUse: A source-faithful vector-reflection explanation is possible; a native illustration requires separately declared apparatus.
cases.answerCompleteness: Not claimed by the executed engine in this trial.
cases.provenanceLimits: Do not label a manually calculated vector answer as a native or registered-engine result.

sourceFacts: Object O is enclosed by three equal-length mirrors AB, BC and AC in an equilateral triangle; figure marks 60 degrees.
Question asks number of images.
sourceUnknowns: No length or exact object coordinates; diagram scale must not supply them.
cases.supportedSubset: Multiple plane-mirror ray tracing can illustrate a fully authored section; counted rays are not enumerated virtual images.
physicalInputsMissing: Metric triangle/source coordinates and emission choices.
cases.educationalUse: Illustrate repeated reflections only with declared geometry; do not equate depth-limited trace with total image count.
cases.answerCompleteness: Image-number question not answered by this engine trial.
cases.provenanceLimits: No finite ray/depth count is proof of a complete image set.

sourceFacts: Two plane mirrors have unsigned inclination 70 degrees.
Ray reflects first at mirror 1 then mirror 2; final direction is parallel to mirror 1.
Requested first incidence angle theta.
sourceUnknowns: Signed mirror orientation, outgoing parallel sign and finite positions are not specified.
cases.supportedSubset: Existing reduced plane-mirror angular query enumerates signed configurations and output signs.
physicalInputsMissing: Finite mirror/source coordinates and optical emission needed only for native verification.
cases.educationalUse: Relate sequential reflection to incidence while explicitly retaining conditional interception.
cases.answerCompleteness: Pending analytical result; no native interception claim.
cases.provenanceLimits: Mirror order is stated by the problem, not discovered by a native inverse solver.

sourceFacts: Concave mirror; object distance is 1.5 times focal-length magnitude.
Object height 2.5 cm is perpendicular to principal axis.
Find image height and erect/inverted orientation.
sourceUnknowns: Absolute focal length and aperture unspecified; absolute focal length is not needed for normalized magnification.
cases.supportedSubset: Existing normalized Gaussian/paraxial curved-mirror image query, with explicit paraxial model choice.
physicalInputsMissing: Finite native mirror geometry, emission and absolute focal scale.
cases.educationalUse: Show normalized magnification without inventing focal length.
cases.answerCompleteness: Pending analytical height/orientation result.
cases.provenanceLimits: Paraxial conditional image mapping is not detected native image formation.

sourceFacts: Ball swings axially before a concave mirror, x = f cos(omega t), with origin at centre of curvature.
Figure's positive x points away from the mirror.
Requests image distance as a function of time, coincidence with object, and lateral magnification at T/2.
sourceUnknowns: f, omega and T are symbolic, not numerical; absolute aperture/emission absent.
cases.supportedSubset: Normalized curved-mirror image query can check selected derived phases with u/f = 2 + cos(omega t), but does not implement arbitrary symbolic motion.
physicalInputsMissing: Absolute physical scale and time/emission choices for native animation.
cases.educationalUse: Check u/f = 3, 2 and 1 at phase 0, pi/2 and pi; preserve focal singularity at the last phase.
cases.answerCompleteness: Selected phase checks are not the full symbolic time-dependent solution.
cases.provenanceLimits: Phase substitution is an explicit source-derived calculation, not a hidden numerical choice for f or omega.

sourceFacts: Concave mirror focal length 20 cm; point object initially on principal axis at 25 cm from pole.
Object speed 5 cm/s at 45 degrees, moving toward mirror and upward as drawn.
Find instantaneous axial and transverse image velocity components.
sourceUnknowns: No native aperture or illumination; stationary mirror/fixed focal length are modelling assumptions for the instantaneous Gaussian derivative.
cases.supportedSubset: Existing curved-mirror image-velocity reduced-facts query.
physicalInputsMissing: Native mirror aperture and source-emission settings; not needed for reduced paraxial derivative.
cases.educationalUse: Use explicit local front-positive coordinate: object axial velocity -5/sqrt(2), transverse +5/sqrt(2) cm/s.
cases.answerCompleteness: Pending conditional image-velocity result.
cases.provenanceLimits: This is instantaneous ideal/paraxial mapping, not native image-motion measurement or propagation delay.

sourceFacts: Object is 100 cm inside water, viewed from air nearly normally.
Find apparent depth.
sourceUnknowns: Neither water nor air has an explicit numerical refractive index in the supplied image.
cases.supportedSubset: New planar apparent-depth API supports an explicit paraxial limit once source/observer indices are declared.
physicalInputsMissing: Numerical source and observer indices. No silent substitution of 4/3 or 1.
cases.educationalUse: Explain the parameter-dependent paraxial relation; a 75 cm result would require an added water-index convention.
cases.answerCompleteness: No numerical original-question result claimed without that stated convention.
cases.provenanceLimits: This is missing numeric authoring context, not evidence that planar apparent-depth physics is unsupported.

sourceFacts: Plane-parallel plate has refractive index 1.8 and thickness 6 cm; it rests on a plane mirror.
Upper-face incidence is 60 degrees from the drawn normal.
Find separation between entry and eventual exit after mirror reflection.
sourceUnknowns: Exterior index, finite lateral dimensions and native source/emission are not numerically specified.

physicalInputsMissing: Declared exterior index, fully explicit mirror/interface/source geometry and physical policies for native illustration.
cases.educationalUse: Trace refract-reflect-refract in a separately completed teaching apparatus; do not fabricate missing exterior medium or full plate geometry.
cases.answerCompleteness: Round-trip displacement not claimed from an executed original-source scene.
cases.provenanceLimits: A source-derived central-ray sketch is not a fully specified native apparatus.

sourceFacts: Glass slab has spatial index mu = sqrt(1+y); thickness d is symbolic.
Incident ray is grazing; origin is the entry point.
Find internal trajectory and exit coordinates.
sourceUnknowns: Numeric thickness and dimension convention for y absent.
cases.supportedSubset: No registered gradient-index propagation in the audited homogeneous planar/finite-glass contracts.
physicalInputsMissing: A supported continuous-index model and its units, not a guessed uniform index.
cases.educationalUse: Explicitly distinguish curved gradient-index paths from piecewise homogeneous refraction.
cases.answerCompleteness: Not answered by this native engine trial.
cases.provenanceLimits: Do not replace the graded medium with an unvalidated stack of homogeneous slabs.

sourceFacts: Three parallel layers have n1=1.60, n2=1.80 and n3=1.30.
Ray begins in medium 1, crosses medium 2 and reaches medium 2/3 at the critical angle.
Find initial theta and describe transmission when theta decreases.
sourceUnknowns: Layer thickness and source placement unspecified; neither is needed for the angular invariant.
cases.supportedSubset: Existing critical-input-angle reduced planar facts query, including decreasing-incidence condition.
physicalInputsMissing: Thickness, native source coordinates/brightness and reflection policy for actual propagation.
cases.educationalUse: Relate invariant n sin(theta) across parallel interfaces to the critical boundary without inventing dimensions.
cases.answerCompleteness: Pending analytical angle and stated decrease condition.
cases.provenanceLimits: An exact-critical analytical result does not certify native completion at grazing emergence.

sourceFacts: Isotropic point source at depth h below water surface; water index mu is symbolic.
A floating opaque disc must hide the source; asks minimum disc radius.
sourceUnknowns: h and mu are symbolic; exterior index not numeric.
cases.supportedSubset: A 2D TIR cross-section could illustrate a declared parameter instance; a three-dimensional escape cone/disc visibility condition is not an observed detector count.
physicalInputsMissing: Explicit parameter instance for any native illustration; 3D/symbolic visibility interpretation remains separate.

cases.answerCompleteness: No minimum-radius visibility claim from this engine trial.
cases.provenanceLimits: A two-dimensional line blocker or zero detector count cannot prove all-direction invisibility.

sourceFacts: Parallel rays hit the flat face of a half-cylinder at 45 degrees in a cross-section normal to its axis.
Glass index sqrt(2); asks conditions avoiding TIR.
sourceUnknowns: Cylinder radius and entry-position distribution are not numeric; exterior index absent.

sourceUnknowns: Inside index is requested, exterior index unspecified; slightly above critical is not an exact equality.
Diagram segment angles without labels are not measurements.

physicalInputsMissing: Explicit limit/approximation interpretation plus material/finite geometry before a native illustration.

cases.answerCompleteness: No unique numerical inverse result claimed.
cases.provenanceLimits: Do not silently replace slightly-above-critical by exactly critical, or use diagram scale to determine the unlabelled internal angle.

sourceUnknowns: Prism angle and index are unknown; exterior index and finite geometry absent.

physicalInputsMissing: Declared small-angle modelling convention, supported joint inverse and independently complete native prism/beam geometry.
